== Overview ==
This shrine is located on Mount Karakai in Ōtsu-chō, Kitaibaraki City. According to shrine tradition, during {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}}'s eastern campaign, his fleet was caught in adverse waves for several days. One night, the deity appeared in his dream, saying, "I am the deity of Sawawa. I have come to protect your ships. I will calm the winds immediately." Upon awakening, the winds had indeed calmed. Yamato Takeru dedicated offerings and enshrined the deity on Mount Sawawa. The shrine became revered as a protector of maritime traffic, earning the name "Karagai no Miya" ("Shrine of Returning from Tang").

In 1869, it was Ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} but was later demoted to {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1871. In 1880, it was reinstated as a gōsha.

=== Deities ===
The main deity is {{ill|Kamo no Okimi|ja|天日方奇日方命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amahikata Kihikata no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鴨王 (上古)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55809532}}. Other deities enshrined include:
- {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944}}
- {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}
- {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主命|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qid=Q10936701}}
- Hime Tatara Isuzu-hime no Mikoto
- Isuzuyori-hime no Mikoto

=== Grounds ===
The honden, built in 1727 during the Kyōhō era, is of the nagare-zukuri style with a copper roof. The former haiden, constructed in 1878, was dismantled in 2018, and a new haiden was completed in 2019.

File:Sawawachigi Jinja Otsucho Massha.jpg|Massha (Inari Shrine)
</gallery>

=== Ofune Festival ===
The spring festival is held once every five years, known as the "Ofune Festival," spanning May 2–3. In 2017, it was designated an {{ill|National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6573893}} by the Japanese government under the name "Hitachi Ōtsu no Ofune Matsuri."

=== Access ===
* location: Ōtsu-chō, Kitaibaraki City, Ibaraki Prefecture
* From {{ill|Ōtsukō Station|en|Ōtsukō Station|qid=Q5353392|lt=Ōtsu Port Station}} (JR Jōban Line), walk 30 minutes east.

== Overview ==
This shrine is located on the slopes of Mount Shiobara in Hanakawa-chō, Kitaibaraki City. According to tradition, Yamato Takeru worshipped the Sawa deity here on his return journey from his eastern campaign. Initially located on Mount Sawa, about 4 kilometers northwest of the current site, the shrine was moved to the mountain summit in 1569 and later relocated to its present position on the slope.

=== deity ===
The enshrined deity is Amahikata Kihikata no Mikoto, also known as:
- Atatsukushinimikoto (阿多都久志尼命)
- Takemisakasawayanosonuminomikoto (速甕之多気佐波夜遅奴美神)
